svg.title: Two cross-field candidates closed at their first review
svg.desc: A two-column ledger of rejected candidates with their checks, prior art and unrun steps, a bar chart of authorship attribution after formatting, and what each failure leaves behind.
svg.text: PLATE III-12-2
LIA / PART III / III-12 CONNECTIONS THAT FAILED
Two cross-field candidates closed at their first review, before any data were
touched
Each was closed with the same verdict. The ledger keeps what was checked, what was found already published, and what was never
run, so the next investigator does not repeat the excavation.
KILL-NOVELTY + KILL-SPECIFICATION + DEFER-CORPUS
CANDIDATE ONE
A ratio law for normalization
Information theory joined to editorial normalization: when text or code is
standardized, the ratio of producer-linked information to remaining uncertainty
should move in a set direction, depending on whether a human editor or a mechanical
rule did it.
Algebra
For the ratio to rise the numerator must fall proportionally less than
the denominator; the candidate’s own falsifier required the opposite.
No universal sign follows.
Specification
Attention versus rule was not identified: editors follow rules, and
autoformatters run rules that people designed.
Prior art
Already measured and published (chart below).
Not run
No corpus acquired, no intervention performed, no mutual-information
estimate fitted.
Kind
false: its algebra ran backwards; its qualitative core was textbook
material
CANDIDATE TWO
Survey weights for surviving archives
Survey-sampling estimators carried into archives: weight each surviving item by the
inverse of its probability of surviving, to correct the distribution of features among lost
items.
Estimator
Unbiased for totals when inclusion probabilities are known and
positive; it does not make nonlinear quantities such as entropy
unbiased.
Specification
Survival is not a probability sample. Items destroyed because of their
features cannot be restored by reweighting the survivors.
Prior art
Green, McIntyre and Needham modeled survival of incunables by
format and leaf count; Lahti, Mäkelä and Tolonen modeled collection
coverage by gender, genre and time.
Not run
No corpus acquired, no propensity fitted, no feature distribution
estimated. A test bed of deleted Git branches proved unrecoverable.
Kind
impossible to resolve from survivors alone
The effect the first candidate would have tested, already measured
Authorship attribution on a paired corpus of 590 Python files by 59 authors, Balla, Gabbrielli and Zacchiroli 2024
original files
formatted
minified
Attribution fell with formatting, with signal remaining. Bars run from zero to 100 percent.
What each failure leaves for the next investigator
Google Flu Trends: compare any new proxy with lagged official data, and check whether the process generating the proxy is stable.
Constraint distillation: the corrected algebra, the citations to read first, and a narrower replication that reports the two quantities separately and infers nothing about attention.
Survival weighting: the conditions under which reweighting is legitimate, and a narrower audit of one observable selection stage, such as which cataloged items were digitized.
Some candidates will be false, others trivial, and others impossible to resolve without new observations.
Sources: Project stage-zero review files for the constraint-distillation and survival-ascertainment candidates; Balla, Gabbrielli and Zacchiroli
2024, as cited in the first file. Neither file records a lag.
